text: 🇲🇽🌎 Mexico to Washington: drop the steel and aluminum tariffs. "I'm optimistic we can reach a deal where we don't keep tariffs on aluminum and steel." — Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, Aug 24 Marcelo Ebrard is in the US negotiating; Sheinbaum expects clarity this week amid the USMCA review. She has answered Trump by letter on tariffs — pressing for dialogue, on terms of mutual respect and sovereignty.

🇲🇽🎨 37,503 university places. No entrance exam. No fees. "In the last two years, 245,111 new places were created in public universities." — Mario Delgado, Education Secretary, mañanera Aug 24 From tomorrow the Educación Superior 2026 platform offers 37,503 spots — 18,674 in-person, 18,629 online/hybrid — to students who didn't place at UNAM. Of 191,069 direct-access applications in the Valle de México, 93.9% got a first or second choice. Education as a right, not a lottery.

🇲🇽🐄 Mexico reopens cattle exports to the US — and Sheinbaum's reminder: the shutdown cut both ways. "We'll open the border, because the border closure also hurt the United States." — Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, Aug 24 After ~22 months of on-off closures over the screwworm, Sonora resumed cattle exports today through the Agua Prieta–Douglas crossing at 750 head a day. Mexico runs full traceability and breeds sterile flies to stop the pest. Chihuahua crossings follow.

📈🇲🇽 <u>Mexico posts its strongest quarter since 2021</u>

INEGI confirms Mexico's GDP grew 1.4% in Q2 2026 — its most dynamic quarter since 2021 — even under Trump's tariff pressure. Agriculture led the first half at +2.1% and services rose +1.1%, a print El Financiero credited as the economy "despunta" despite the trade war. Not the collapse Washington's analysts kept forecasting.

🎶🇲🇽 <u>México Canta takes on the narcocorrido — now with Spotify</u>

Sheinbaum's México Canta, a binational contest for artists aged 18–29, is rewriting regional Mexican music away from narco-glorification — and Spotify just joined, adding official playlists, a masterclass for the 14 semifinalists and industry access for the winners. The road to the final runs from LA (Aug 23) to Mazatlán, closing at Mexico City's Auditorio Nacional on Sept 13.
banner: MEXICO CANTA + SPOTIFY VS NARCO SONGS

🌽🇲🇽 <u>A US firm's RNA pesticide gets its first-ever green light — in Mexico</u>

Mexico just became the first country on Earth to approve an RNA-interference biofungicide from US biotech Green Light Biosciences, waved through by Cofepris on a fast track. The scientists behind the GM-corn fight — the Sin Maíz No Hay País coalition — warn it breaches the constitutional precautionary principle, with no scientific consensus on its safety for pollinators, soil microbes or entire food webs.
banner: US RNA PESTICIDE: SCIENTISTS SOUND ALARM

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Mexico to US: stop routing our deportees through third countries</u>

Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez told US Ambassador Ronald Johnson that Mexico won't accept its nationals being sent through Guatemala, Honduras or Costa Rica before reaching home: "we don't accept that our compatriots be transferred to a third country before arriving in Mexico." She noted irregular Mexican migration to the US has already fallen 96%.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Harfuch: no foreign forces operate on Mexican soil</u>

As Washington floats "military options" against the cartels, Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch drew the line: "It's not about whether we want it — our law does not allow foreign forces in our country." Cooperation means shared intelligence, not US agents running operations here; the capture of "El Mencho," he noted, was carried out 100% by the Mexican Army.
banner: MEXICO: NO FOREIGN AGENTS ON OUR SOIL

text:
🇲🇽🐄 <u>US reopens its border to Mexican cattle after 14 months</u>

After 14 months sealed over a screwworm outbreak, the US reopened its border to live Mexican cattle today, starting at Agua Prieta, Sonora. The fix wasn't a wall — it was science: a sterile-fly plant in Chiapas, co-financed by both governments, that SADER is now scaling up to wipe out the pest. More than a year of Mexican-led coordination reopened a market Washington shut unilaterally.

<u>LA TIMES</u>: Did Mexico create a "blacklist" of journalists and politicians?
August 21, 2026 | 🟡

A presidency official projected a slide of critical journalists and opposition figures at the morning press conference. LA Times put the opposition's "enemy list" charge in the headline — then, to its credit, quoted Sheinbaum flatly denying any intent to censor.

Left out of the frame: the slide ran in the government's official "right of reply" segment rebutting specific coverage — not a secret dossier, a distinction the word "blacklist" erases.

• Sheinbaum, in 2021, on the same idea: "Who makes lists? McCarthyism, Nazism, fascism."
